name: Wolne Lektury
licence: Wolna Sztuka 1.3 (ex-CC BY-SA), per-book; public domain for pre-1955-death authors
access_method: public REST API https://wolnelektury.pl/api/ (JSON/XML, no key) + plain txt/html/epub/pdf per book
value_for_task: high: clean editorial text + metadata (author/epoch/genre) for primary-source excerpts (e.g. Kazania sejmowe, pamietniki) used in matura source-analysis questions
reason: clean text + open API + explicit reuse licence; best effort/value ratio of all sources checked

name: Wikizrodla (Polish Wikisource)
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (wiki text) / public domain (original documents)
access_method: MediaWiki API (api.php, same tooling as pl.wikipedia.org) + full XML dumps on dumps.wikimedia.org
value_for_task: high: full constitutions (1791/1815/1921/1935/1952/1997), treaties, and category Dokumenty_historyczne give primary sources the CKE informator explicitly tests (source-analysis questions)
reason: same ingestion pipeline already built for kb/ (Wikipedia dump); just point it at the plwikisource dump

name: Wikidata
access_method: public SPARQL endpoint (no key) + REST API + JSON dumps
value_for_task: high: deterministic chronology/ordering/matching questions (reign dates, battle dates, treaty dates) generated straight from query results -- verified working, see wikidata_polish_rulers_sample.json
reason: zero copyright risk (CC0); caveat: raw position-held queries return noise (pretenders/claimants never crowned) so results need qualifier/rank filtering before use as ground truth

name: Federacja Bibliotek Cyfrowych (FBC)
type: national aggregator/index of 130+ Polish digital libraries
licence: varies per source library (metadata mostly open Dublin Core; underlying objects mixed, incl. all-rights-reserved)
access_method: OAI-PMH harvesting (open, no key) + OpenSearch + CSV export of provider list
value_for_task: medium: the master index of which Polish libraries hold which digitised historical books -- useful to point download scripts at, not itself a text source
reason: answers 'portal indeksujacy ksiazki historyczne' literally, but only yields metadata/pointers; turning a hit into clean usable text still needs a per-library OCR/rights check

name: Polona (Biblioteka Narodowa)
licence: per-object: marked public domain / CC0, or all-rights-reserved, on each item page
access_method: web UI + IIIF image API + developer API via https://cpa.gov.pl/store/apis/info?name=polona (registration/token required)
value_for_task: medium-high: largest single collection of scanned historical Polish books and press, but delivered as page images -- needs OCR and a per-item licence check before reuse
reason: huge legal corpus in principle, but no bulk clean-text export; per-item licence variance + OCR effort make it a stretch goal beyond a 40-min timebox

name: Encyklopedia Orgelbranda (1859/1872/1898)
url: https://pl.wikisource.org/wiki/Indeks:S._Orgelbranda_Encyklopedia_Powszechna_(1859) (scans also on Polona / Cybra Lodz / Jagiellonska BC)
licence: public domain (published 1859-1898, all authors long dead)
access_method: Wikisource transcription = same MediaWiki API/dump route as wikizrodla row; scans on regional libraries need OCR
value_for_task: low-medium: definitional/terminology content only -- 19th-c. spelling and pre-1945 historiography do not match the CKE informator's modern interpretive framing
reason: real public-domain text exists and is reachable via the Wikisource route with no extra tooling, but archaic language + outdated historiography limits direct use for matura-style questions; treat as stretch/background corpus, not primary

name: dane.gov.pl (Otwarte Dane) incl. "Pomniki historii"
licence: Polish public-sector-information reuse law; per-dataset licence stated on its page (many CC0/CC BY)
access_method: REST API (api.dane.gov.pl/doc) + per-resource APIs, e.g. https://dane.gov.pl/pl/dataset/168/resource/35931 (Pomniki historii)
value_for_task: low-medium: narrow fact source (legally-protected historic-site names + decree dates) -- useful for a small slice of matura content, not general history-book text
reason: legitimately open and API-driven, but the exact dataset schema could not be rendered in this pass (page needs JS); verify api.dane.gov.pl/doc directly before building on it

name: KRONIK@ (Krajowe Repozytorium Obiektow Nauki i Kultury)
type: new (2025) unified national digitisation repository (~4.5M objects)
licence: stated by MC press release as "per licence conditions, most often public domain"; not verified per-item in this pass
access_method: web portal; a partner-only integration API is mentioned in MC materials but no public self-serve API was found
value_for_task: unknown/medium: potentially large future source once book-level content and a public API are confirmed
reason: too new / no public API documentation found in this research pass; re-check post-hackathon before relying on it

name: Europeana
type: pan-European cultural-heritage aggregator (includes FBC's ~2.1M Polish records)
licence: ALL metadata CC0 1.0; underlying digitised objects carry per-item rightsstatement.org codes (InC / NoC-NC / Public Domain Mark / CC0 -- check edmRights field)
access_method: free self-service REST API key at https://api.europeana.eu/en
value_for_task: low-medium for this task: mostly redundant with FBC/Polona for pure-Poland content; useful only for cross-referencing or non-Polish-partner treaty documents
reason: good licence hygiene (CC0 metadata + explicit per-item rights) but low marginal value over FBC/Polona already covering the same Polish libraries

name: IPN -- Przystanek Historia / Biblioteka Cyfrowa IPN
type: ~800 free-to-download PDFs (books/bulletins/exhibition catalogs) from Institute of National Remembrance
licence: all rights reserved (c) IPN -- confirmed on-page; free download does NOT mean free reuse
access_method: plain HTTPS download links; no API
value_for_task: would be high (curriculum-aligned 20th-c. history, matches CKE's post-1945 focus) IF licence allowed reuse
reason: classic legal-access-but-no-reuse-licence trap the hackathon rules warn about; do not put in repo or train on -- at most a human fact-check reference, never bulk-downloaded by script

name: Project Gutenberg (Polish shelf)
licence: PG License (public domain / free redistribution with standard header)
value_for_task: low: Polish-language subset is small and mostly literary fiction (Mickiewicz, Sienkiewicz), not history textbooks/monographs -- fiction is not a safe ground-truth fact source for exam answers
reason: legally clean but wrong content type for a fact-generation task; only viable as a background language corpus, not as a source of verifiable historical facts

name: Internet Archive
type: global scan archive (incl. controlled digital lending)
licence: mixed per item -- ranges from true public domain (downloadable _djvu.txt) to Controlled Digital Lending (borrow-only, DRM'd, NOT redistributable)
access_method: metadata + advancedsearch API; full text only for public-domain items
value_for_task: medium in principle, but the top search hit for "Polish history" (Zamoyski, Poland: A History) is CDL-only -- easy to accidentally grab a non-free item
reason: real risk of violating the hackathon legal-access rule if the rights field is not filtered per item (mediatype:texts AND rights "Public Domain"); skip given the timebox

name: Google Books API / HathiTrust
type: commercial book search / US academic full-text repository
licence: Google Books ToS forbids bulk scraping of in-copyright snippets; HathiTrust full-text access outside member institutions is restricted to US-public-domain items and requires a Data API partner agreement
access_method: Google Books API (metadata/snippets only) / HathiTrust Data API (partner-gated)
reason: terms of service explicitly forbid the access pattern this task would need (bulk/automated full-text download); direct rule violation of do-not-download-from-sites-whose-terms-forbid-it
